title: Weighted mismatch and small-ball bound
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\{-1,1\}$, and let $\ell$ be a real-valued function on that cube. For $t\geq0$, define the threshold sign to be $1$ when its argument is nonnegative and $-1$ otherwise. Then $2t$ times the uniform probability that $f(x)$ differs from the threshold sign of $\ell(x)$, minus the uniform probability that $|\ell(x)|\leq t$, is at most $\mathbb{E}[(\operatorname{sign}(\ell(x))-f(x))\ell(x)]$, where the expectation is uniform on the cube and $\operatorname{sign}(\ell(x))$ denotes that threshold sign.
hypotheses_covered: $\ell$ is real-valued on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
